notes.title: Konkwest Patch 1.0042
notes.notes:
With this patch several bugs were fixed and the 1900 scenario was improved.


 Sokoto and Dendi, two pre-colonial West African countries, were added to the 1900 scenario.
 Fixed war declarations being absent from the history and news.
 Added a short cooldown to popup buttons, to counteract players unintentionally closing multiple popups when trying to close just one.
 Fixed misaligned tooltips at resolutions significantly different from 1920x1080.
 Fixed conquer-n-places button showing up for countries with which you have a truce.

notes.title: Konkwest Patch 1.0041
notes.notes:
This small patch fixes the following issues in the game:


 Desyncs happening when the NPCs try specializing their regions (pretty much every turn)
 Flickering border outlines
 Hesse (a country in Germany) being missing in 1700


Have a great time conquering the world!

notes.title: Konkwest Update 1.004
notes.notes:
This is a small update fixing some issues with the game, and making some changes to the world.

Feature
You can now invite other, non-enemy countries, to try joining institutions that you are a part of.

Scenarios

 The HRE in 1300 has been turned into an institution and its member states were added as countries.
 Added institutions to the 2000 scenario.


World

 Aceh, Brunei, Champa, the Mekong Delta, and Singapore have been added as places.
 Changed several water places in the Atlantic Ocean.


Performance

 Improved performace by making several smaller changes:
 Enhanced the performance of NPCAI.SpecializeARegion.
 Removed one unneccessary call to CountriesSystem.UpdateCountriesAttitudeLists per turn.
 Improved performance of NPCAI.MakePlans.


Bugs
Fixed a bug where united political unions (in particular NATO) could generate country IDs that were too long to be playable.
Removed a false entry in the list of options for starting votes in your institutions.
Fixed improve relations hotkey.
The UI listing which countries voted for and against decisions in the institution screen now properly uses localized country names if available.
Fixed a bug where truce requests would not arrive in the inbox of the target country.

Other

 Institution members will now dislike countries that attack their fellow members.
 Updated the app icon.
 Improved the flag of Majapahit.
 Added an example institution to the example mod.
 Lowered the border-line-elevation to decrease the visual gap notable in close perspectives sometimes.
 If you are at war with a country and, because of alliances, can't directly make peace with them, you will now see a text explaining how you can, or who can make peace.

notes.title: Konkwest: Diplomania Update (v 1.003)
notes.notes:
This update for Konkwest overhauls the game's entire diplomacy system! (v1.003)
Instead of the ternary neutral / friends / enemies system, countries now have more granular relations to one another, on a scale from 0 to 100. Special treaties, unions and organizations are now represented in the game as Institutions.

Diplomatic Requests
Accepting and denying diplomatic requests now influences your relation to the countries that sent them, and sending them can cost power. Countries' relations are also influenced by their expansions, conflicts and agreements. Additionally, countries with the same traditional language group tend to like each other more.

Diplomatic requests that don't make a difference will no longer be received, so you practically won't get spam-mail from the other countries anymore.

Institutions
You can create an institution and choose aspects for it. The available institution aspects are:

 Association: Improve your relation to the other members over time.
 Internal peace: Members can't fight each other.
 Military access: Members can attack non-members through each other's territory.
 Alliance: Members automatically defend other members if they get attacked.
 Political Union: Allows the institution to unite into a new country.


Main Menu
The main menu background has been exchanged for a dynamic scene showing the game world and a flag. When you play as a country it will show your country and its flag.

Map Modes

 Added an institutions map mode, where countries that are part of the same institutions have the same color. Countries that are part of multiple institutions get the average color of their institutions' colors.
 The diplomatic map mode shows countries that share important institutions with the selected country using stripes.
 Uncolonized land is now terrain-colored instead of black or beige in the diplomatic and political map modes.


Regions
Regions can now stretch across up to one water place, which makes it no longer required to have a unique region for each island.

Scenarios

 Adjusted many of the scenarios to make use of the new features.
 In the 1700 scenario the Holy Roman Empire has been turned into an institutions and the different member states are now their own countries.
 Improved historical accuracy in the 1900 scenario, especially in North Africa, where the Sultanate of Agadez was added.
 Improved historical accuracy in the 1300 scenario, where the principalities of Smolensk and Vladimir were added.
 The default scenario is now 1700, because it is easier to get to know the game in an age where diplomatic complexity is lower than contemporarily.


Netcode
Updated the Photon Fusion networking package to version 2.0.1. This should fix a lot of the random occurrences of "unexpected network errors" that used to be a nuisance.

Other

 The find-a-place feature has been improved, so that you can now enter partial names of places, regions or countries, and get a list of relevant search results to select from.
 The atmosphere shader has been replaced with a better one from a plugin developed by Kai Angulo.
 If the autosave feature is enabled the game now automatically loads your autosave on startup.
 The flag shader has been improved.
 Most flags have been replaced with higher resolution, more detailed versions.
 The grassland terrain color is now more green, making it more visible next to desert.
 The tutorial makes reference to the new diplomatic mechanics.


Bugfixes

 Fixed a few keybinds not working properly.
 Fixed a lot of bugs that would have been added to the game with this update if they hadn't been fixed.


Known Issues

 Countries at war can use military access granted to their enemies. This is intended, but there is currently no visual indication of that, so it can be confusing.
 The 2024 & EU scenario is now redundant but still included in the game.
 The 2000 scenario does not yet feature any institutions.
 Some of the new update has so far only been translated automatically. If you find issues with the translations feel free to let me know.

notes.title: Year Zero & Multiplayer Update for Konkwest
notes.notes:
Konkwest version 1.001 brings Ancient times to the game! Additionally it is now easier than ever to set up and find a multiplayer match!

Scenarios

 New Scenario: 0 (1BC) - Challenge the great ancient empires of Rome and China, or lead them to world domination!
 The new scenario also comes with flags for all the countries in it. Those are all either from a future time period or fantastical, since countries / peoples did not actually use flags back then.
 Added flags for Siam (Thailand in 1900), Lan Xang (1700), and Khmer Empire (by Khnom) (alternative).
 Added ECOWAS as a friend group to the 2000 and 2024 scenarios.


Multiplayer
Added a new main menu button, with which you can join a random multiplayer game. When you start a new multiplayer game you can now choose whether or not you want to allow random players to join using that new feature.

Music
Added new track "Dealings of the Diplomat" by Leon Richter to the game soundtrack.

Localization
Added an extensive Spanish translation by Luz Blanco Davelaar and Porfirio Osuna.

Other changes

 Added a button linking to the Discord server into the main menu.
 Linguistic promotion and repression effects no longer divided by amount of promoted or repressed languages.
 Languages are no longer actively promoted beyond 90%.
 Conquering places now adds up to 5% of your country's traditional language to them.
 East Libya and West Libya now have the Libyan flag.

notes.title: Flags & Shields Update in Konkwest
notes.notes:
This update adds flags and shields to the game, but also a huge load of other content.

Flags and Shields

 All countries in Konkwest, if they historically had a flag, have a flag now, which is displayed in various places throughout the game, for example on a shield displayed on each place on the globe, and on a flag on each country's capital.
 Flags are linked to the country name. If you rename your country it will adopt the flag matching the new country name if given, or use the country's color as the flag.


Gameplay

 Countries can no longer spawn back in if their traditional language is not at least present by 5% in their origin place.
 Countries can now start at war or with active friendships in the starting scenario.
 When you select regions or countries, that will now be visually represented by the selected places moving upwards.


Chat
There is now an ingame chat where you can communicate with the other players in your game room.

Netcode

 Almost the entire netcode of Konkwest has been rewritten to be more reliable. In case of connection interruptions players with connection issues will now automatically be switched to single player mode. If a player who is a game room's master client disconnects, another player will now automatically replace them.


Scenarios

 In some starting scenarios countries now have diplomatic relations from the start. This means some countries start as friends, while others start at war.
 As of this update, this models as friendships (in 2024): ASEAN, the East African community, the EU, the Inter-American Treaty, the Iranian sphere of influence, Mercosur, NATO, the neutrality of Switzerland, and the Union State.
 As of this update, this models as wars (in 2024): the Libyan civil war (with current truce), the Russian invasion of Ukraine, and the Yemeni civil war.
 New scenario: 2024 + EU
 More countries have been added to the Balanced scenario and the Alternative Counties scenario.
 Scenarios can now include occupied places.


Lighting
Place markers are now affected by lighting, with the exception of capital stars and flags.

Linguistics

 Improved the linguistic simulation, so development of languages over time behaves more as one would expect.
 Each country can now have a local variant name for it's traditional language group. This way, Latin in France will be called French and Latin in Honduras will be called Spanish. While this is not quite how it works in the real world, it does add a bit more flavor to the simulation.
 Traditional languages in historical scenarios will now be boosted before countries spawn, so that historical countries won't automatically adapt to the modern language distributions.


Localization

 Translated country names and demonyms.
 Dozens of other new translations.
 Konkwest should now be fully translated in German and Dutch.


Performance
Removed several issues causing lag spikes between turns.

User Interface

 The load a game menu now displays details about the different saved games before you load them.
 The game status note is now in the bottom right corner instead of the bottom middle of the screen. It now also displays more accurate status information.
 Place labels are now a bit smaller and have a lower display range.
 There is a button to lower all fortification in a region of yours or even your entire country.

notes.title: World update
notes.notes:
With this development update, Konkwest is now almost ready for release. A release, which unfortunately won't be coming as soon as I hoped it would. I had a multiplayer playtest session yesterday and there are still a number of relevant bugs to be fixed. I have therefore moved the expected release time for the game to May 2024. When Konkwest comes out I want every player to have a great time building their empire!

World

 Corrected elevation data for Asia, Africa, Australia, and Oceania so these continents now appear with more correct elevation in the game.
 The more a place's industry is developed, the more of a city appears there visually.
 Arabia: Added one additional place each to Yemen and Oman.
 China: Split Hebei into Northern, Southern, and Western Hebei, so it won't be as easy to defeat China by surrounding Beijing.
 Pakistan: Split Pakistan's former two places into four new ones: Eastern Balochistan, Sindh, Western Punjab, and Northern Pakistan.
 Uzbekistan: Created Karakalpakstan as a new place in western Uzbekistan.
 Sudan: Created the place Northern Sudan by splitting it off from Port Sudan.
 Tibet: Split Tibet into the places Tibetan Plateau, Himalayas (East, Center, and West), and Kunlun.
 Xinjiang: Created, in addition to the places Dzungaria and Tarim Basin, a new place for the Tian Shan.


Map modes

 New: Power per Country: This map mode colors the countries based on how powerful they are.
 New: Players: Only countries played by players in multiplayer are highlighted.
 Updated colors for neutral countries and places without country in the diplomatic map mode.


Music

 Added a new piece to the soundtrack: "A Palace for Spies" by Leon Richter.


NPC AI

 There are now difficulty options for the AI: easy, hard, and mixed. With the mixed settings some countries will use the easy AI settings, and some will use the hard ones.
 NPCs use the mechanics to change the region of places and to unite regions to expand their main region.
 NPCs unite their regions sometimes.
 NPCs send and answer truce requests more reasonably.
 NPCs typically target smaller countries when deciding who to attack.
 NPCs use regional specializations.


Game Mechanics

 There is now a button to develop industry in a specific region.
 Improved automatic naming for new regions.
 There is now a victory screen when only one country remains in the world, with a celebratory popup and fireworks.
 Added a filter for inappropriate words when naming things.
 Regional specializations now default to appropriate ones.


Netcode

 You can now choose "Automatic" as your server region (which is also the new default option).
 Improved player list synchronization.
 Improved player ready status synchronization.
 Improved player country synchronization.
 If plan submission in multiplayer fails for over 10 seconds the plans of players who didn't submit (due to a network issue) will be ignored.
 De jure country IDs are now synchronized when new countries spawn.


Keyboard shortcuts

 You can use Esc to open or close the main menu.
 You can use Enter to accept popups.
 You can use Backspace to decline popups.
 You can use the keys shown in tooltips to access specific functions in the game, when the respective buttons are visible, such as space to ready up and c to conquer.


Localization

 Place names on the globe now support Arabic characters.
 Added more translation content.


Android

 Reduced the size of the adaptive app icon foreground element to better fit typical display formats.


Bugfixes

 You can not attack a country immediately after making peace anymore.
 The People's Republic of China, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Democratic People's Republic of Korea now have correct abbreviations.
 The develop industry in country button can no longer target level 10 places.
 Two NPCs can no longer remain on the world peacefully forever.
 Players joining a multiplayer game will now correctly stop playing their singleplayer country.
 When there are n players in the game and n-1 players are ready, the game no longer advances unintentionally.
 After peace agreements with land exchange the affected countries now perform an integrity check and label adjustments.
 When making a white peace the larger country now always returns land to the smaller country before the reverse.
 Fixed an error occurring when an attacker, winning a war through a peace deal, receives no places.
 You can immediately start playing a newly created custom country again.
 If the game detects a desync you will no longer stay in spectate mode.


Known Issues

 The turn timer is broken. It first causes some strange glitch and then two turns happen at once if it expires.
 Creating custom countries causes the game to soft lock.

notes.title: Tutorial Update
notes.notes:
Konkwest now finally has a tutorial!
It's not complete yet, but it should be when the game is released.

Tutorial

 Added a tutorial mechanic with a basic and intermediate chapter. (Advanced chapter should follow.)
 Added a popup asking if you want to see the tutorial when starting a new game.


Simulation

 Stability now slowly ticks up, even when a place is not under any country's control.


Localization

 Diplomatic requests are now fully localizable.
 Some of the game is available in French.
 Fixed various minor error occurring due to use of uninitialized localization variables.


Netcode

 Improved game synchronization in multiplayer.
 Implemented a desync detection mechanism that informs players if the game desynchhronizes. This can help fix bugs, and reloading the latest save file should always allow players to continue where they left off if they happen to desync. (If your multiplayer game desyncs, please let me know on Discord to help make the game more stable.)


User Interface

 Changed the multiselector design (used to switch between interaction layers in the location panel, and in the news screen) to better accomodate different screen sizes.
 Fixed: Tooltips in arabic script don't disappear when they should.
 Fixed: Instead of part of the plan description to create a custom country being colored, it included the color code.

notes.title: Important Bugfixes, Regions, and Localization Improvements
notes.notes:
This update brings important bugfixes to Konkwest, and adds to the game's localization.

Regions

 Regional specializations have been refactored. (Earlier versions of this update caused this to make it impossible to load savegames with regional specializations. This is fixed now, and old savegames, even ones corrupted from that bug, should load just fine.)
 The agriculture specialization, instead of a flat +7 bonus for fields, now provides a +25% bonus for fields, grassland, and hills.


Localization

 Made almost 40 popup texts localizable with German and Dutch versions already available.
 All content of the region view and the country view is localizable (except names).
 Added right-to-left script support for country labels on the globe.
 The place power info popup is fully localizable.
 All popups caused by the place view are localizable.
 The linguistic policy screen and all its content (except names) is localizable.


Multiplayer

 Fixed a bug where, when a client started playing a country, that didn't exist on another client's local machine, because the game is in the process of loading something, would lead to a soft-lock of the game.
 Fixed a bug where, when any player renamed a place to an invalid value, all players in the game would see the error message, instead of just the player who tried the renaming.
 Fixed a bug where the game would soft-lock if a player leaves and their ID is not locally registered (for example when they join and their connection is so bad that they instantly disconnect).


Touchscreens
When pinching to zoom you no longer accidentally cause orbital camera movement.

User Interface

 Your plans' power cost is now shown in the "Your plans" panel.
 The place power info popup now includes information about the impact of local stability and fortifications on the power output.
 Buttons don't flash in spectate mode anymore.
 Added an icon to the settings button and the select language button to indicate where to find the language settings in case you can't read the language the game is currently in.
 Fixed a bug where you could not see your diplomatic requests, because the button wouldn't show up.
 Fixed a bug where automatically generated plan data could cause a display error in the place view, leading to many missing buttons.


Android
Updated app icon for compatibility with newer Android versions.

notes.title: Graphics Options Update
notes.notes:
Konkwest now has graphics options, where you can select from four quality levels:

minimum: as the name suggests, this one comes with nothing special
low: default on Android; this one has 4x Antialiasing, which is an important improvement over none
high: default on Windows; this one has shadows (3 shadow cascades)
ultra: this one has 8x Antialiasing, better shadows (4 cascades), and renders in 1.25x superresolution


UI

When you receive diplomatic requests or when you plan something, a red circle effect now highlights the appropriate buttons.
New graphics for the power bar.
There is a marker for requesting ownership of a place now.


Map Modes

Added a regions map mode, which shows the regions of the selected country in colors, and the specialization of each region striped.


Help Articles

Added new help articles about these topics: capitals, countries, de jure ownership, places, regions, terrain types


Bugfixes

 Possibly fixed a bug that soft-locks the game when a transmission fails in multiplayer. (I couldn't test this yet, since that requires someone with an unstable connection.)
 When creating a custom country, the previous country no longer retains de jure ownership of the place.
 The player country panel no longer glitches out at low display or window heights.
 The leaderboard remains visible when ready.
 All plan execution effects occur as planned again (industry development gears were missing).
 Loading a game no longer resets custom place names.
 You can no longer name your country " " (spaces).
 The turn timer uses the correct font.

notes.title: Polish, Music, Netcode and Rockets Update
notes.notes:
In Konkwest expansion actions are now symbolized by exploding rockets instead of just explosions.
Also there is a lot of new music implemented!

Netcode

The game no longer soft-crashes when the host disconnects from a multiplayer game.
The multiplayer system works as intended again using room codes, which are now properly used and enforced.
Cross-platform multiplayer between Windows and Android is confirmed functional.


User Interface

Long tooltips are now displayed across multiple lines instead of running over the edge of the screen.
The multiplayer button is correctly labeled when in multiplayer.
Tooltips, the place UI, and multiselector options now support Arabic script properly.
Help articles no longer glitch out near the screen edges when scrolling.
It is now possible to open the power info for places with no country and for places with no power.
The loading screen can show the mountain image from the leaderboard.
The "Enter player name" popup opens after the loading screen instead of during it.
No longer showing a popup that a new game started. (Because it's obvious.)


Localization

More content added to the Arabic localization.


Balancing

Terrain types now have a stronger impact on takeover costs. (All modifiers doubled.)


Scenarios

The 1700 Jesuit Order state now correctly respawns in South America instead of France.
Added Atlantis as an alternative country.
Corrected the Demonym of Hejaz to Hejazi.


Optimization

Places are no longer accidentally selected when trying to drag.
terrain shader allows for direct texture application
added elevation data for Asian places with A
